items.title: After mainlining 30 hours of 1440p Bloodborne, I know in my heart it belongs on PC
items.summary: You can force it, but it shouldn't be so unapproachable.
items.content:
Gaming After mainlining 30 hours of 1440p Bloodborne, I know in my heart it belongs on PC PC Gamer Follow Ted Litchfield Thu, September 24, 2026 at 8:17 PM UTC When you buy through links on our articles, Future and its syndication partners may earn a commission.

I decided to finally take fate into my own hands. Bloodborne is one of my favorite games of all time, and it is the only one I have spent a significant amount of time playing on the Sony PlayStation 4. I resent that. I hate that horrible little box under my TV with a passion. I think it's only good for watching Gilmore Girls⁠—I don't like playing videogames on it. I am a PC man through and through.

Enter the shadPS4 emulator and BB Launcher , two wonderful tools for running this wonderful game on PC. I followed YouTuber Retro Renew 's guide to emulating Bloodborne, and we were off to the races.

Sekiro, Elden Ring, and Armored Core 6 are all-timer games for me. Crucially, they've demonstrated continued growth and a willingness to experiment on the part of FromSoftware. I don't think the studio "peaked" with Bloodborne by any means, or that its best days are behind it, but there is nothing else out there like it.

The atmosphere and aesthetics of Yharnam are still so striking and odd, like if Nosferatu (pick your version) and Lovecraft were chopped and screwed into black metal album art. It applies the surreal, mythic sensibility of FromSoftware to the modern world, resulting in the most dreamlike, alienating narrative the studio has yet created.

The Healing Church and Byrgenwerth are simultaneously ancient and right there . Master Willem, the primeval progenitor of Cthulhu Studies in this world, is still chilling in a rocking chair on his front porch. Byrgenwerth, a distinctly modern-feeling Cthulhu University, predates the Healing Church. There's this feeling Yharnam regressed from science and study into religious dogmatism, clad in modernity and enlightenment the entire time. But the scientists who created this sickened modernity are hardly blameless, no matter their intentions. Does this remind you of anything?

One reading I had never heard before tuning into the recent Chapo Trap House Players Club episode about Bloodborne is that it's a game about motherhood and mothers, and men ruining the world by doing terrible things to them. It seems so obvious to me now. Kos and her orphan, Queen Yharnam and her child Mergo: The crimes committed against these mothers are the inciting events of the story. You can do the same to Ariana and her child, in the hopes of becoming a god.

God the combat . I fought Ludwig the Accursed earlier than I ever have this playthrough, and it taxed me like little else I've played recently⁠—I felt weirdly shaken afterward. While this is the smallest arsenal of the post-Demon's Souls FromSoft catalogue, every weapon is fully distinct from one another⁠—with the exception of one baffling, fighting game-style moveset clone . Nobody playing Elden Ring would go to the mat for the Highland Axe or Torchpole , but every weapon in Bloodborne has at least one freak out there who will say it's their favorite⁠—I'm a Chikage / Saw Cleaver man, myself.

Bloodborne emulation has been better than the original console experience for some time, but it's still slightly janky. I find "unpatched multiplatform Unreal Engine 5 triple-A port" to be a good comparison point: Basically, the hitches and glitches reminded me of playing Jedi Survivor.

You'll need a beefier rig than for other PS4-era games, and it isn't like there are minimum and recommended specs online anywhere. But I've been surprised at the GPUs I've seen people running Bloodborne on, with one Reddit commenter claiming it was playable on a GTX 1650. I don't have a way of testing, but my wager would be that the RTX 3070 (or equivalent) is the point where you could start expecting reliable 1080p 60fps gameplay.

Digital Foundry demonstrated 4k 60fps gameplay on an RTX 4080 earlier this year, while I've had a pleasant experience at 1440p 60 on an RX 9070 XT from AMD. There's only one glitch that has really spat in my coffee, and I don't have a fix. I've run into two loading zones⁠—the entrance to Yharnam's Grand Cathedral and the elevator depot shortcut in the Forbidden Woods⁠—where, seven out of 10 times, stepping through a doorway turns my field of view into a neon nightmare until I quit and reload.

Reader, I have tried nearly everything to troubleshoot: Tweaking resolution, VRAM use, shadPS4 versions, lighting settings, FSR use, the gamut. I don't know if it's a Bloodborne on PC thing, or a fromsoftserve BB Remaster mod thing. The only option left is doing a full reinstall, and that just doesn't feel worth the effort for this edge case annoyance. I simply choose to accept it as a quirky old friend now, like having to slam the dashboard of an old car just so to get it to run.

I have always refused to be the kind of sucker who pays Sony to let me use the internet I already pay for (the PlayStation Network), so I never really interacted with Bloodborne's online-only procedurally generated dungeons. The PC BB Launcher has a function to force-add procgen dungeons to your save file, and comes with a library of popular ones for loot/experience farming.

I didn't even realize there was a whole sequence of story-based, set Chalice dungeons to explore prior to now⁠—it's possibly FromSoftware's least intuitive, most poorly explained system in any of its games, putting Demon's Souls world tendency to shame.

items.summary: Dark Souls 2 seamless co-op is nearly here
items.content:

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 0 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Modder Yui has become a legend in the FromSoftware community after developing seamless co-op mods for Elden Ring, Dark Souls, and Dark Souls 3 . But don't think the middle entry in the series is dodging a similar treatment, even with its controversial reputation among the fandom. Dark Souls 2 seamless co-op is coming very soon, complete with proximity chat and an array of quality-of-life tweaks.

Dark Souls 2 seamless co-op is set to be released on Tuesday, September 22, as Yui explains in a Patreon post . Don't let that link worry you about it being stuck behind a paywall, either, as the mod will also be available on Nexus Mods and GitHub.

As with most of FromSoftware's games, Dark Souls 2 technically has co-op, but the summoning system is even more restrictive than in its siblings. The seamless co-op mod will make it fully playable, start-to-finish, with your friends. It includes proximity chat for both co-op partners and invaders, though both forms of it are optional.

As Amirah, who also worked on the project, explains in a video breaking down the mod, there is "synchronized progress and no interruptions. Dying, defeating a boss, or going through a loading screen won't kick anyone you've summoned out of the session." Progress carries back to the worlds of summoned players, too.

Watch On Dying in seamless co-op doesn't actually reset the world state, so there's a unique new mechanic to keep you from abusing this fact. Each time you die, you'll get a cursed soul fragment, with each instance of the item carried by your crew slowly powering up your enemies. Resting at a bonfire to reset the enemies will also reset your soul fragments. This mechanic is also optional, but it should help preserve the game's challenge.

How Elden Ring multiplayer and playing co-op with friends works Metal Gear Solid is getting co-op after 28 years thanks to "world first" mod FromSoftware enters the SBMM debate with The Duskbloods, and plans on having ranked matchmaking There are also general quality of life improvements here that should make Dark Souls 2 more pleasant to play. The controller dead zone has been improved. A double clicking issue that introduced apparent input lag for mouse and keyboard has been addressed. Perhaps most notably, limited-time event content is now accessible "at any time."

It's all reason enough to give Dark Souls 2 a modern reevaluation. I don't have strong feelings about Dark Souls 2 – it's the one entry in the trilogy I haven't played – but my coworkers assure me that its negative reputation is well deserved ( editor's note: it's good, but doomed to be compared to the greats) and I will definitely not be inundated with comments from fans who believe it's unfairly maligned as a result of the above headline. Hopefully you'll all be too busy with co-op to bother.

He's been covering games (with occasional dalliances in the worlds of anime and pro wrestling) since 2015, first as a freelancer, then as a news writer at PCGamesN for nearly five years. items.title: ‘Elden Ring’ saved Serena Cherry’s life – so she made an extreme metal album about it
items.summary: "The challenge of that game taught me not to give up on myself"
items.content:
Noctule’s Serena Cherry. CREDIT: Serena Cherry

N octule, the solo project of former Svalbard vocalist Serena Cherry, doesn’t fit neatly into the rules of black metal. Instead of raucous anthems about Satan and the Norse landscape, her upcoming second album ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ is all about fantasy game Elden Ring – the nightmarish epic filled with scary monsters and snarling beasties that’s sold more than 30million copies since its release in 2022.

Elden Ring’ s sprawling, open-world adventure is soundtracked by sparse, brooding instrumental music – but instead of channeling that, Cherry has smashed together the heavily-distorted, outrageously heavy genre of black metal with the more melodic, but no less forgiving melodeath (AKA melodic death metal) for ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’, which is out September 25. It’s bigger and meaner than Noctule’s ferocious debut, which paid homage to 2011’s nerdy spells, swords and dragons role-playing game Skyrim .

“You look at most metal album covers and they look like something from World Of Warcraft , or vice versa,” Cherry tells NME from her living room, surrounded by Noctule vinyl and t-shirts ready to be sent out to fans. “Not many people are chucking on a metal album when they’re doing the washing up, it’s not a passive listen. You’re meant to [play] it loud and let it totally overcome you, in the same way that you get immersed in the world of video games.”

Noctule, like a lot of DIY bedroom projects, was born during COVID . Cherry had lost her day job in retail and her evenings were freed up thanks to a ban on live gigs. She had first started experimenting with black metal as a teenager – using a tape recorder and a “crappy” drum machine to create rudimentary demos in her bedroom – and had always wanted to revisit the genre. Now, stuck at home amid the enforced unemployment of lockdown, she could do just that.

Another of Noctule’s early influences was the aforementioned Skyrim , which she considers one of her favourite ever games. Returning to the rich world of Tamriel during COVID meant Noctule’s first songs soon became “an ode to one of the greatest role-playing games of all time.” Full of crushing breakdowns, screamed vocals and soaring electric guitar licks, it’s the type of music you’d want playing if you were going up against a one thousand-year-old Dragon Priest with anger issues. Cherry had no plans to release the tracks, but some friends talked her into putting ‘Wretched Abyss’ out online. She was “blown away” by the enthusiastic response: “It reassured me that extreme metal still has those corners that are open to something that doesn’t follow the rules.”

Progress on follow-up ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ has been slower going – cobbled together in spare moments on Svalbard world tours between 2023 and 2025. “I’ve got a whole bunch of voice notes on my phone of me singing riffs in a toilet in Australia,” Cherry says, clearly enjoying the creative control her new project offered. “We all contributed in Svalbard so I’m used to hearing ‘no’. With Noctule, I could do what I wanted and nothing could stop me.”

I f Noctule’s first album was a tribute to Skyrim , then her second set of sinister thrashers owes a debt to Elden Ring . “‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ was my way of saying thank you to a game that I attribute to saving my life. I was so depressed just before it came out, and it gave me purpose and gave me strength,” says Cherry. “As soon as I started playing it, I knew I had to write about it.”

Usually, it’s cosy games such as Animal Crossing and Stardew Valley that get brought up during conversations about gaming and mental health – but Cherry finds their overly cheery escapism grating. “There’s comfort in art that’s unapologetically bleak,” she says. “Sometimes you just want to sit in the darkness… Elden Ring isn’t afraid to be unflinching in the way that it paints this world where everything is in turmoil. There’s a hopelessness to it.”

This hopelessness is felt most keenly during the many fiendishly tricky fights with merciless monster bosses – and this really drew Cherry in. “I’m not naturally that great at video games,” she says, “but with Elden Ring , everything about it was so tough that it brought out a stubbornness in me that’s actually quite healthy.” That same stubbornness now pushes her to go to the gym and to pursue her musical projects. “The game is basically a stern parental figure that motivates you to keep going. Writing this album was a celebration of the challenge that those bosses represented.”

After the lush, instrumental opener ‘Welcome To Limgrave’, which refers to the game’s open-field starting region, each ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ tune is about a different Elden Ring boss. And with more than 200 to choose from, Cherry had to be selective – only including her absolute favourites. It’s not pure fantasy though. “There are lyrics where I’ve drawn parallels between the lore of certain bosses and my own life,” she explains. Recent single ‘Goddess Of Rot’ is about the incredibly difficult, sword-wielding badass Malenia. “She’s such a tragic character but remains so defiant and loyal. The whole idea of loyalty that turns into a punishment is something I connected with.” ‘Lord Of Blood’ is a liberated rager about the towering, horned hulk Mogh and the meme-inspiring serpent Rykard also has his own song. Another track is about spurned and banished demigod Morgott, who was cast out by his family: “That reflects in me [because] I’ve never really felt part of the metal scene, in a lot of ways,” says Cherry, who’s previously spoken about gender inequality in heavy music.

“Using characters as a way to explore your thoughts and feelings makes you feel more protected than if you’re just speaking plainly,” says Cherry. It’s something she experienced first-hand while recording all the vocals for ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ in a single night. “With Svalbard, I usually ended up crying in the vocal booth. With Noctule, I had this big stance and I was belting out the screams. Sometimes you get moments when you’re creating music where you just feel bigger.”

‘Extinguish Thy Flame’ isn’t the first Noctule record, but it’s the first thing Cherry has released since Svalbard played their final ever show last month after more than 15 years as one of the most beloved metal bands in Britain. “Financially and life-wise, it was unsustainable to continue,” says Cherry. “It’s awkward to be one of those small to mid-sized bands. You’re releasing albums and touring as much as possible, but you’re not making any money from it so you all need to have full-time jobs. The balancing act was becoming incredibly stressful and draining. And that’s a quick way to ruin your dreams. It was impacting our creativity as well, so my outlook was that the only way for it to change was for it to end.” Cherry now feels like she has “everything to prove” with ‘Extinguish Thy Flame’.

As well as inspiring more metal fans to check out Elden Ring , Cherry hopes people can “draw a sense of fight and courage” from the project. “It’s very much an aggressive album that’s got its chest puffed out,” she says. “The whole experience was about finding the joy in creating music again – and celebrating the game that got me through the toughest times of my life. If this album has a similar impact on others, that would be amazing.”

items.title: Elden Ring Nightreign is dead, but modders are dabbing on its corpse, with one porting an entire Dark Souls 2 DLC zone as a playable map
items.summary: A new spin on an old favorite.
items.content:

(Image credit: FromSoftware) {alert('Link copied')}).catch(err => {console.error('Failed to copy: ', err)})" data-platform="copy_link" data-action="" class="font-ui-heading py-2 text-sm text-neutral-700 hover:bg-neutral-100 transition-colors no-underline block cursor-pointer border-0 bg-transparent w-full text-left normal-case" aria-label="Copy link" role="menuitem" data-analytics-id="article-social" analytics-label="utility-bar-social-share-copy-link" analytics-name="utility-bar-secondary" data-mrf-recirculation="article-social"> Copy link Facebook X Reddit Pinterest Flipboard Email Share this article 33 Join the conversation Follow us Add us as a preferred source on Google Newsletter Subscribe to our newsletter Modder Doneda has released a particularly funky and exciting mod for Elden Ring Nightreign, porting Dark Souls 2's Frozen Eleum Loyce and Frigid Outskirts as a standalone map. They also have a trailer up for the project on YouTube. Doneda's a bit of a Dark Souls 2 expert⁠—they previously restored the remains of a cut sewers map to the sequel for demonstration purposes.

Watch On Gun to my head, I think the Brume Tower is my favorite DS2 level, but Eleum Loyce still feels like a dear old friend. I enjoyed base DS2 more than most, but the Lost Crowns DLCs were on a whole different level. Other FromSoft DLCs may be better in a vacuum (Old Hunters, Shadow of the Erdtree), but there has never been a more staggering, exhilarating leap in quality between one of the studio's games and its corresponding expansion.

While Brume Tower may be my beautiful baby, it just wouldn't fit in Nightreign like Eleum Loyce does: The wide open Outskirts and walled city can mimic the mini open world of Limveld in a way the twisty, narrow Brume Tower couldn't manage. My favorite detail is that it looks like the night two circle narrows down on the underground chaos arena where you fight the Burnt Ivory King , a fun and creative recontextualizing of the level's original flow.

Doneda's new map is already available for download on the Nightreign Nexus. You'll need to install Mod Engine 3 beforehand to run it⁠—most, if not all Nightreign mods require the utility. Doneda seems intent on making more modded Nightreign maps, and you can follow their work on YouTube or support them via Ko-fi .

You talk about love/hate relationships, I'd say I have a ⅔ hate, ⅓ love relationship with Nightreign. Its Deep of Night update gave me and my friends incentive to keep playing, while it introduces some truly incredible boss fights⁠—stuff like The Balancers and Libra give me hope that FromSoft can still surprise, delight, and challenge in a post-Promised Consort world.

Elden Ring's Tarnished Edition is exciting enough on its own, but it's also our last chance to properly experience the game's launch day hype Elden Ring players are hard at work putting the new Tarnished Edition DLC's gear to the test I'm a decade-plus FromSoftware sicko, and these are my 5 takeaways from the first Duskbloods gameplay But Deep of Night also subjected us to the most frustrating, artless version of FromSoftware difficulty I've yet seen, and the studio appears to have quietly stopped supporting the game to work on The Duskbloods⁠—and hopefully something else, too?

Perhaps I should take the glass half full view of FromSoft releasing a multiplayer game, supporting it a bit, but not feeling compelled to turn it into a forever empire of live service returns. In the absence of official support, though, there have been some weird, exciting things happening with Nightreign. Yui's Nightreign iteration of her signature Seamless Co-op mod is a welcome addition for more "chill with your friends" -style play, while I've been intrigued by gameplay videos of TerraMag's SotE and ds3 weapons , a "no duh" addition that I'm still surprised FromSoft didn't manage itself.

items.title: New Elden Ring Mini Replicas Arrive: Malenia, Messmer & Wylder
items.summary: Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the l
items.content:
Tarnished, collectors, and champions of the Lands Between, we're excited to unveil a new lineup of premium 1/3 Scale Mini Replicas inspired by some of the most iconic designs from the Elden Ring universe and crafted by Pure Arts. From the legendary Blade of Miquella, to the fearsome Messmer the Impaler, and the indominable warriors of Nightreign, these finely crafted collectibles capture the artistry and atmosphere that have made the Elden Ring universe unforgettable.

Elden Ring - Arm of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Celebrate the unmatched elegance and strength of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this exquisite 1/3 scale replica of her prosthetic arm from Elden Ring. Meticulously sculpted and finished, the piece highlights every refined detail - from the intricate golden engravings to the articulated armor plating that defines her graceful yet deadly form. The arm's metallic sheen and subtle weathering evoke the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior. Presented on a simple black display base, it offers an elegant way to showcase this symbol of unwavering resolve.

Elden Ring - Helmet of Malenia Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Honor the legacy of Malenia, Blade of Miquella, with this meticulously crafted 1/3 scale replica of her legendary helmet from Elden Ring. Every detail reflects the beauty and ferocity of the demigoddess warrior, from the intricate engravings to the elegant winged crest that defines her unmistakable silhouette. The helmet's metallic finish and subtle weathering capture the essence of Malenia, Blade of Miquella's battle-worn armor. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant and timeless way to display this symbol of strength and determination.

Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree - Helmet of Messmer Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Embrace the dark majesty of Messmer the Impaler with this finely detailed 1/3 scale replica of his distinctive helmet from Elden Ring: Shadow of the Erdtree. Sculpted with precision, the piece captures the menacing elegance of Messmer the Impaler's design - from the elongated horns and ornate patterns to the burnished metallic finish that reflects his fiery power. The helmet's intricate craftsmanship evokes the regal yet fearsome aura of the Impaler himself. Presented on a simple black display stand, it provides a refined presentation worthy of this symbol of divine wrath.

Elden Ring Nightreign - Helmet of Wylder Mini Replica (1/3 Scale)

Enter the shadowed realm of Elden Ring Nightreign with this finely crafted 1/3 scale replica of the Wylder Helmet, an iconic piece of armor worn by the wandering knights of the darkened lands. This high-quality collectible captures every intricate detail of the original design, from the weathered metallic finish to the subtle engravings that mark its storied past. The helmet features a fabric neck veil, adding texture and realism to the piece. Presented on a simple black display stand, it offers an elegant way to showcase its imposing form.

Expand Your Collection

Each of these officially licensed mini replicas has been crafted by Pure Arts to faithfully capture the spirit, craftsmanship, and legendary designs of the Elden Ring universe. Whether your allegiance lies with Malenia, your fascination belongs to Messmer, or you're drawn to the mysteries of Nightreign, these collectibles are the perfect way to bring a piece of the Lands Between to your collection.

Which replica will earn a place on your shelf?

items.title: An Obscure Setting Keeps Ruining Elden Ring: Nightreign For Me
items.summary: I do not want to know about any of this
items.content:
I have over 150 hours in Elden Ring Nightreign , and as I have admitted before on this website, I am not very good at it. Over the course of that 150 hours, I think I’ve spent a lot of time being carried by both my partner and our trios pal, who plays Guardian consistently and is great at making sure my wimpy Recluse/Scholar-ass doesn’t die (or, when dead, gets revived promptly). Together, we have taken 150 hours to very slowly kill almost every regular Night Boss in the game, leaving just the DLC’s Dreglord unslain at this time. It is likely due in no small part to my lack of skill that it has taken this long, though I also somewhat blame our busy lives and the fact that we often take long breaks and forget how to play.

But earlier this week, I have found another culprit to pin this on, and her name is Nat. NAT Type.

What the hell is NAT type? I’m still not 100-percent sure despite it being explained to me repeatedly. From what I can gather, it’s some mysterious, internet-related setting that determines how online games connect to the internet and to other people playing those games on the internet. I had literally never heard of it prior to Monday of this week, and I wish I still didn’t know about it.

The reason NAT type came up is because both my partner and I have been having constant issues with disconnects in Elden Ring Nightreign for several months now, for seemingly no particular reason. Almost every single match, one or both of us would disconnect. First, there would be up to 20 seconds or so where our characters would be stuck running around the world, unable to do damage or affect anything in them. Then, we’d actually get kicked out, and have to go through the grueling process of getting back to the menu screen, clicking through some menus, and then reloading back into the game. And because it’s Nightreign , this would be a huge disadvantage. We’d end up wasting something like a full minute of time, and when we got back in we’d either respawn somewhere vaguely near where we disconnected, with all our runes (including one whole lost level) dumped somewhere else for us to go waste time picking up. Or, if we were at the end of a night, we’d just respawn dead, and whoever was still connected would have to maneuver over to us while still fighting the boss and try to get us back up.

This has been infuriating! I tolerated it for a long time, because I enjoy Nightreign , but it really, really feels bad to be the one dragging the group down in this manner.

We tried everything to fix it. Whatever solution you’re about to suggest, we did it. We checked our connections. We reset the router so many times. We changed who hosted the match. We screwed around with all sorts of settings. We made sure we were on wired connections. Etc etc etc. None of it worked.

Finally, my partner did some dedicated research and discovered that something called our NAT type was the problem. Apparently, our NAT types were set to Moderate, which can cause issues with online multiplayer. From what I can figure out, you can change your NAT type properly by following a bunch of complex steps dealing with your router. Or for us on Xbox, we were able to spam the “Test NAT” function in the settings until eventually it swapped our NAT type to Open. When we played hours later, my partner’s was fixed, but mine was not. We checked the settings again, and mine had reverted back to Moderate. We spammed Test NAT again, got it to Open, and we’ve had uninterrupted matches ever since.

So I guess now before I play Nightreign , I have to check this setting every time? This is ridiculous! Why does stuff work like this? I feel like I shouldn’t have to do deep research into an obscure-for-most-people internet setting just to play an online game as it’s intended to be played. I’m not trying to do anything wacky here, I’m literally just getting into a co-op game with two other people, all of whom have excellent internet connections. Most people should not have to know about NAT type, or UPNP (whatever that is) or IPV6 or any of the other weird acronyms I saw while researching this. Like yes, I could probably work this out with time if I sat down and messed around with it long enough, but I don’t have time to do technological research just to bonk a stupid death goop monster around a giant arena without making my friend solo him for 60 seconds at a time at random.

If you’re having trouble with disconnections in Nightreign or Elden Ring PvP stuff or anything like that, consider melting your brain and learning about NAT type. I don’t recommend it, but it did result in me being able to play Nightreign without (unnecessary) frustration, improving my evenings dramatically. However, as soon as I beat up Dreglord, I intend to forget everything I know (very little) about NAT type again for the rest of my life.

items.title: Elden Ring Tarnished Edition Review – A Masterpiece in Your Hands
items.summary: The Elden Ring Tarnish Edition brings together the beloved ARPG and its excellent DLC as one package for the Nintendo Switch 2.
items.content:
Back when it was released in 2024, I gave Elden Ring a score of 98. Four years later, and considering I have well over 1000 hours of play time on PC and PS5, I still wonder if my score was too low. For me, Elden Ring is the absolute pinnacle of FromSoftware’s design philosophy and the gold standard for open world action games. It’s now hard to put myself in the shoes of someone playing Elden Ring for the first time. Considering that around 30-40% of Switch 2 owners don’t have a gaming PC or other high-end console, there’s a good chance that gamers picking up the Tarnished Edition will be dropping in for the first time. Lucky them.

The Tarnished Edition brings together the base game and Shadow of the Erdtree DLC, itself maybe the best DLC ever released for a game. It also includes a handful of new weapons, two new classes, and skins for Torrent, the player’s mount. These add-ons are also available for $4.99 for PC and console games who already own the game. Accessing the game’s co-op and PvP features means having a subscription to Nintendo Switch Online.

If you’ve already played Elden Ring on PC or another console, you’re probably just wondering how it fares on Nintendo Switch 2. Elden Ring on the go sounds like a dream come true. The good news is that it runs just fine, if you’re willing to accept some limitations. Frame rates are capped at 30fps. Textures and ray tracing are a little simplified and a bit blurry, especially in handheld mode. On the other hand, the beauty of Elden Ring is in its art, character and environmental designs. It doesn’t depend on photorealism. In combat, the 30fps throttle is a little more frustrating, and framerates dip a little in the more intense boss battles. Bottom line, the Switch 2 is powerful enough to run Elden Ring and players will have the full experience.

If you’ve never played a FromSoftware game, be prepared for some narrative confusion. The developer is known for stories that are opaque, dense with lore and full of sadness, darkness, and fading hope. With an assist by George R.R. Martin, Elden Ring’s narrative tells of a shattered world. The demigod children of Queen Marika have torn the realm apart. The player takes on the role of a Tarnished, tasked with slaying the corrupt demigods and claiming the title of Elden Lord.

It should be noted that with any FromSoft game, there are fans who dive deep into the lore. At the other end, there are even more players who simply ignore most of the narrative and focus on exploration and combat. Elden Ring rewards either approach. For anyone who’s confused, there’s an immense amount of material online about the characters and their complex relationships.

When it comes to action and combat, Elden Ring represents a major step forward and brings together mechanics explored in other games from the developer. There are few — if any — action RPGs with boss battles as finely tuned as those in Elden Ring. The number of weapons, armor sets, and ways to use magic is staggering in its variety. Like most RPGs, Elden Ring has starting classes but these are largely ignored by players past the first few hours. That said, the Tarnished Edition adds two extremely viable classes in the form of the Heavy Knight and Idus Knight.

Souls games have a well-earned reputation for difficulty, and FromSoftware has resisted adding difficulty options. That’s because they’re built in. Especially in Elden Ring, if players are struggling there are always areas to visit and lower level enemies to kill. There are other weapons or spells to try. The game’s system for summoning Spirit Ashes allows players to call on extremely competent AI companions to help out. Compared to exacting platformers where there is no margin for error, FromSoft’s games feel, if not forgiving, at least balanced and fair.

Outside of combat, exploration is extremely rewarding thanks to a fast travel system and Torrent, your mount. While Elden Ring’s map isn’t the biggest open world it feels immense due to layers of verticality and subterranean areas to explore. No area feels too empty and between the labyrinthine Legacy Dungeons and open landscapes, there’s always something to discover or fight. The Shadow of the Erdtree DLC added a significant amount of new content to an already massive game.

If you haven’t played Elden Ring, and the Tarnished Edition on the Switch 2 has enticed you, please make the leap. I envy you seeing it all for the first time. If you have the game on other consoles or PC and don’t own something like a Steam deck or ROG Ally, the Elden Ring you love is there and intact, but with the visual downgrade that you probably expect. In the end, more Elden Ring is a very good thing.

***Switch 2 code provided by the publisher for review***

items.title: HoYoverse's 'Elden Ring Meets Monster Hunter' Actually Plays More Like Final Fantasy 16
items.summary: Nodusfall has some unexpected points of comparison
items.content:
By Ari Notis Published Aug 30, 2026, 6:43 PM EDT Ari Notis is deputy editor of games at Polygon, where he oversees the gaming section. Previously, he was Polygon’s guides editor. Prior to joining Polygon, he was a reporter at Kotaku, the popular gaming site, and a senior editor at the lifestyle publication Best Life. He also served in various editorial capacities at various Hearst publications, including Esquire, Veranda, and Metropolitan Home. Ari is one of the people who still play Halo Infinite on a weekly basis. There are dozens of them! Gamescom Nodusfall charts new territory for the Genshin Impact maker

Image: HoYoverse Nodusfall Sign in to your Polygon.com account Add Us Summary Generate a summary of this story Like Like follow Follow followed Followed Thread 2 Log in Here is a fact-based summary of the story contents: Try something different: Show me the facts Explain it like I’m 5 Give me a lighthearted recap Zenless Zone Zero . Honkai: Star Rail . Genshin Impact . You probably know HoYoverse for its signature anime-inspired aesthetic and mobile-friendly games. But the international gacha powerhouse is expanding its purview in the coming year with a slew of games that don’t neatly fit into its existing oeuvre. One of those is the monster-slaying action game Nodusfall , revealed during the 2026 Gamescom Opening Night Live showcase.

Nodusfall stood out as one of the more unexpected reveals of the show. Gone was the typical HoYo aesthetic, instead favoring a photorealistic graphics style, anchored by a visual language more reminiscent of FromSoftware’s dour, gothic vibe than anything the company has produced before. Nodusfall was described across the internet, including by this website , as a sort of “Elden Ring meets Monster Hunter” type mashup.

At a glance, sure. But after playing Nodusfall at a hands-on preview during Gamescom, I’m not totally sold on those descriptions. The Monster Hunter stuff? Yes, absolutely. But the Elden Ring comparisons seem to purely exist on a superficial level, at least according to the hour of hands-on time I spent with it.

Image: HoYoverse Nodusfall is a cooperative action game for up to four players. My demo paired me with three other journalists, and we chose from Suixi, an archer; Grahmer, a dude with a giant broadsword; Qiong, another archer; and Gamescom1, your typical sword warrior class, whom I opted to play as. (I learned too late that you can rename your character.) You can also customize which abilities you bring into the field. Instead of going with a purely attack-based loadout, I opted to equip one area-of-effect healing spell. None of us chose a dedicated healer, and it was clear none of us knew what we were doing. The healing spell couldn’t hurt, I figured.

Your base in Nodusfall is a tent village situated on a wooden network of platforms on the side of a steep mountain, tucked partially into some caves. There, you can upgrade gear, interact with merchants, and get quests — which appeared to be of the “go track and hunt this giant monster” variety — from a quest board. It’s all very Monster Hunter-y, minus the cat people.

Combat is much like many other third-person action games: basic attacks, special attacks, dodges, and a unique twist on the parry that so many of you sickos have grown to love these days. But rather than pressing the right button at the right time, you charge up a heavy attack then, right when you’re about to get hit, release the button to “clash” with (i.e., parry) your attacker. You can additionally hold down the right bumper to access four equipped abilities, each tied to its own cooldown. Enacting these moves feels smooth and natural, though the hits don’t land with a ton of weight. The special attacks certainly have more flair. One character wields a flaming sword. Another turns into a flying demon and hurls giant orbs of miasma.

Image: HoYoverse Our first mission, “Purge Evil Spirits,” tasked us with… purging evil spirits. After embarking from camp into the overworld, our party hopped on mounts — fantastical equine creatures who (sorry, Elden Ring fans) apparently can’t double-jump. The first evil spirit we came across was Quongqi, a 30-foot-tall gryphon with three health bars and tornado-summoning powers. As the close-combat sword wielder, I took the brunt of its focus (and quietly thanked myself for remembering to slot the healing spell into my loadout).

As we whittled its health down to about the halfway point, Quongqi ran away. We hopped back on our not-quite-horse mounts and chased after it, eventually bringing it down in the center of a dramatic subterranean lake. When playing co-op, weaken an enemy enough, and you can team up for powerful team attacks called “joint executions.” These moves are flashy as hell: In one, our party summoned a spectral giant who smashed his 30-foot battleaxe into the gryphon’s neck.

Image: HoYoverse The final boss fight of the mission was against a similarly 30-foot-tall dragon named Maldrake. Also, Maldrake had a rider: the suitably named Maldrake Knight, an enormous dude who can summon a 30-foot-tall sword of light. (30 feet seems to be the standard unit of measurement in Nodusfall .) This played out much the same as the fight against Quongqi: three health bars, lots of spectacle. At one point, Maldrake Knight kicked me into the sky, then used his enormous weaponry to pile-drive me into the ground. To quote one of my party members: “That was awesome .”

Elden Ring ’s boss fights obviously have flair, but are meticulous, demanding, patient affairs. Playing Nodusfall , I couldn’t help but feel like I was playing a cooperative mod for Final Fantasy 16 , the divisive series entry that impressed even its biggest haters with those speculator boss fights. Summoning the giant axe-wielding spirit seemed like calling forth an Eikon from Square’s action-RPG. Maybe it’s because I was playing the most Clive Rosfield-like character in the roster, but even the basic attacks felt more like Clive’s reckless sword-swinging than like the Tarnished’s methodical expertise.

This makes sense for Nodusfall , what with its heavy emphasis on playing with other people. If combat in Nodusfall were as technical as it was in a FromSoftware game, it’s not hard to imagine how high-skilled players could get frustrated playing alongside beginners.

Nodusfall is a free-to-play game with a PvP component in the works, but it’s unclear exactly how microtransactions — which have been present in every HoYoverse game to date — will manifest here. In a press release, HoYoverse said that characters will not be obtained through randomized rolls and that additional purchases will be cosmetic in nature, but noted that it’s still fine-tuning exactly how microtransactions will appear in the game.

Nodusfall does not have a release date. HoYoverse said it will “definitely” be released on Windows PC but did not confirm other platforms.

Tarnished Pack Additional Content

  • Added Idus Knight and Heavy Knight as new starting classes, selectable during character creation. Note: The equipment of each new starting class can also be obtained by purchasing it from merchants in the Lands Between or by finding it in the world.

items.title: Elden Ring: Tarnished Edition for Switch 2 means you can now touch grace AND grass
Elden Ring On Switch 2 – The Worst Way To Play The Best Game
items.summary: Elden Ring on Switch 2 gets the job done admirably, but it is the inferior version of a fantastic game. - Game Informer

items.title: Rise with ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition, launching 28th August on Nintendo Switch 2
items.content:
The Lands Between—a place of myth, gods, and broken dreams. Long ago, Queen Marika and her divine offspring reigned here, but since the Elden Ring was shattered, the world has fallen into decay. Now, the land whispers for a King.

The ‘Tarnished’, long exiled, are finally seeing the light of Grace once more. Step into this hauntingly beautiful realm, unravel its ancient mysteries, and rise as the one true Elden Lord.

The ELDEN RING Tarnished Edition game arrives on the Nintendo Switch™ 2 system on 28th August .

The Lands Between are part of a vast continent, where magnificent open fields and huge dungeons with complex three-dimensional designs are seamlessly connected. As you explore, the joy of discovering unknown and overwhelming threats awaits you.

Mastery of the terrain and knowledge of its secrets can help you overcome enemies and defeat formidable bosses—or lead invading players into traps.

An epic drama born from a myth created by George R.R. Martin The founding mythology of Elden Ring was written by George R. R. Martin and adapted into a rich multilayered story. Intersecting goals and desires between the characters create an intense narrative that weaves throughout the Lands Between. The events of the game can unravel in many ways—depending on your interventions.

Combat is simple to learn yet offers hidden depths of dexterity. As you seek to become the Elden Lord, you’ll need to explore the balance between attacking, avoiding damage, using a wide variety of weapons, spells, summons, and perfecting your timing to take advantage of your opponents’ weaknesses.

Create and build your own character In addition to customising the appearance of your character, there are countless ways to combine the weapons, armour, usable items, and magic that you equip. You can develop your character according to your play style.

No matter if you prefer bold physical confrontation, tactical spellcasting, or the subtle art of stealth, you’ll be able to find gear that supports your choices.

Traverse together with other Nintendo Switch 2 players. You can play with up to two other Tarnished as your cooperative teammates, either by inviting them using a shared password or by summoning them from a pool of nearby community members.

There are also ample opportunities to face off against other players, either through co-op invasions, invited duels, or the many player battle options available in the three Colosseums.

If you’d like to learn more or begin your journey to the Lands Between by pre-ordering the Tarnished Edition, please check out the link below.

items.title: What Is Elden Ring About?
items.summary: Discover what Elden Ring is about: a dark fantasy epic by FromSoftware & George R.R. Martin, set in a vast open world. Join 30M+ players and become the next Elden Lord!
items.content:
The legend of ELDEN RING is a dark fantasy epic born from a collaboration between two masters of the genre.

Using the seed of a story about bloodline, heritage and betrayal written by George R.R. Martin , Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware have crafted a vast and beautiful wilderness out of the ruins of a kingdom fractured by war between demigods.

After the assassination of Godwyn the Golden , her oldest son, god queen Marika shattered the Elden Ring that was the source of her power. Her remaining children took up these pieces for themselves. Using the might these runes gave them, the Demigods fought to become her successor, each driven by their own motives.

However, this maddening war was a stalemate with no clear victor. The Demigods retreated to their respective realms as the world fell further and further into stagnation, the Golden Order sundered.

But now, a group of banished warriors known as the Tarnished are returning to the Lands Between . You are one of those Tarnished , the dead who yet live, drawn by the guidance of what grace remains to seek the throne and become the next Elden Lord .

Read more about the story of ELDEN RING’s Age of the Gods, the history crafted by George R.R. Martin and Hidetaka Miyazaki.

The world of ELDEN RING is dangerous and majestic. Pale grasslands lead to flooded plains where dragons roost. A crimson battlefield now seethes under scarlet swamps of rot. You’ll climb frozen mountains, search through mystical forests, conquer golden kingdoms, and that’s only the beginning.

All of these rich landscapes are host to deadly enemies and wonderous secrets. There are caves and deep crypts guarded by traps, forts that have fallen to rebellions, and ruins of past civilizations that are now home to monsters and madmen.

Most intricate of all are the vast legacy dungeons like Stormveil castle , whose ramparts crown the high hills of Limgrave . Many of these sprawling dungeons host the remaining Demigods who guard their Great Runes within.

As you travel, you may also find the few souls who remain in the land still possessed of their wits and intellect. Most still retain their ambitions as well and may ask for your help. Aid or hinder them as you see fit, either way could benefit you in some manner if you are wise.

Prepare to explore the Lands Between with our ELDEN RING Starter Guide.

For over a decade FromSoftware have created an iconic system of gameplay that influenced countless other games. The broader gaming culture has defined titles that take their inspiration from the Souls series as being part of a “Soulslike” genre .

The Souls series has many unique features, but the genre is defined by three main features. All Souls series games have combat focused on precise timing and evasion that is simple to learn but challenging to master.

They also include a system that requires the player to survive between checkpoints at the risk of losing the currency they receive from defeating enemies that is used to purchase stat upgrades. And of course, the Souls series feature intense, memorable boss fights that test the player’s skills to progress through the story.

items.title: ELDEN RING - RAGING WOLF 1/6 SCALE STATUE
items.summary: Who is the Raging Wolf? Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to
items.content:
Who is the Raging Wolf?

Among the first Tarnished to join the Roundtable Hold was Vargram, a warrior of great skill and ferocity. He acquired the title of the Raging Wolf from the white wolf pelt that flowed from his helm. Vargram sought to become the shadow of one of the Empyreans and built his strength relentlessly as he traveled through fallow Limgrave to the golden city of Leyndell. And yet in spite of all his strength, his armor is now worn by another… An unnamed Tarnished now walks the Lands Between in the skin of the wolf. Does this warrior seek the same fate as Vargram, forever stalking at the side of an Empyrean? Will they uphold the Golden Order or supplant it for some new code? Whatever the destination, woe befall upon any who dare block the path.

The most impressive Elden Ring statue yet

Standing at 33 cm/13 inches, it’s one of the largest character statues ever produced for ELDEN RING. Crafted with the attentive supervision of FromSoftware, this full 1/6 scale figure captures each minute detail with masterful skill. The size allows perfect fidelity to the beautiful and dark fantasy atmosphere of the game, including smears of bloody red across blade of the Bastard Sword and the crest of the Iron Roundshield. From the intricate filigrees of its helm to its whisps of silvered fur blown back by an errant breeze to the humble, dusty cloth wraps protecting the feet of its greaves against the mossy stones of the path to Stormveil Castle, it’s a portrait of the implacable will of the Tarnished. All these expertly rendered touches from sculpturer Shinya Yamaoka make this statue a perfect match to the most iconic set from one of the most iconic games of this generation.

Where can I get a Raging Wolf Set statue?

Pre-orders for the Raging Wolf 1/6 scale statue can be placed on the official Bandai Namco website. At this time, based on the production estimates of Gecco studio, these stunning PVC/ABS figures will ship to your home in Winter of 2026. If you are a true aficionado of the game, there is no better purchase to bring the world of Elden Ring to your home or office. It’s a timeless piece for your own collection or an impressive gift for a friend or loved one. And one small note, if you have not yet found this set in the Lands Between for your Tarnished, we recommend you seek the aid of Recusant Bernahl at the Volcano Manor.

Place your order for the Raging Wolf statue on the official Bandai Namco Store.

*This product is available on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, the Middle East, India, and the United States.

items.summary: Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree. Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set
items.content:
Follow in the foosteps of Miquella once more with this exclusive 2 disc vinyl collection, celebrating the sweeping, emotional journey of Shadow of the Erdtree.

Presented with the reverence merited by a legendary expansion, this premium set is crafted for collectors, audiophiles, and Tarnished who seek to experience the Realm of Shadow through its music.

The Collection

Housed in a full color gatefold sleeve and marked with the symbol of Messmer the Impaler, each vinyl disc is pressed on heavyweight material to ensure optimal durability and warmth of playback. Whether displayed proudly on a shelf or played to relive your own quest, this set is designed as both a collector’s piece and a lasting tribute to one of the most celebrated expansions in modern gaming.

The Artists

Across 18 tracks, the soundtrack transforms the ELDEN RING experience into a powerful standalone odyssey—one carried by orchestral grandeur, ethereal choir work, and the signature melancholy that defines the worlds created by FromSoftware.

A Collector’s Treasure

This official vinyl set is an essential centerpiece for any discerning fan’s collection. Perfect for longtime followers of FromSoftware’s musical legacy or newcomers drawn into the Land of Shadow for the first time. *This vinyl is available exclusively on the Bandai Namco Store in Europe, Australia, Middle East, India and the United States
